bindings.label: Patient has spontaneous eye opening without contact and no motor response

65-year-old man with no reported medical history, no treatment at home, completely self-sufficient before admission, arrived at ICU intubated and mechanically ventilated due to loss of consciousness with Glasgow Coma Scale rapidly deteriorating to 3

After initial treatment and recovery, patient experienced multiple complications including acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock events, cardiogenic shock, obstructive shock due to pulmonary embolism, and multi-organ failure requiring hemodialysis

On day 39 of ICU care, after stabilization and lifting of sedation, examination revealed spontaneous eye opening without contact, no motor response, and basic neurological status with no meaningful interaction
Initial CT/MRI showed only right posterior inferior cerebellar artery territory infarct without classic hypoxic-ischemic pattern (cortex, basal ganglia, watershed zones)
Follow-up MRI on day 49 showed no new parenchymal lesions
EEG improved from non-reactive delta waves to reactive theta waves
